purpose: Predeclare the comparator set, clock, and resolution rules for the bounded first-party proposition that high shipping fuel costs hit food prices first.

source_boundary.authorized_text: High Shipping Fuel Costs Hit Food Prices First.
stronger_claims_forbidden_without_transc: specific CPI subindex not named in the source
specific geography beyond the source context

clock.boundary_basis: USDA documented IFO 380 all-time high on March 9 and Global 20 Ports VLSFO at $960/metric ton on March 11, up 79% from two weeks earlier.
clock.rule: Both clocks must remain visible. A favorable result under only one clock cannot erase the other.

ordering_rule.signal_definition: first material post-shock acceleration or persistent elevation relative to the immediately preceding baseline, evaluated consistently across comparator lanes
ordering_rule.minimum_persistence: one monthly observation for a large discrete change or two consecutive observations for small changes
ordering_rule.ties: If food and one or more comparator lanes cross the materiality rule in the same reference month, terminal ordering remains TIED_OR_UNRESOLVED rather than awarding first place.
ordering_rule.mixed_food_rule: Food-at-home and food-away-from-home are reported separately. A rise in one cannot silently substitute for the other.
ordering_rule.causal_rule: Ordering score does not establish shipping fuel as sole or dominant cause.

anti_hindsight_rules: Do not add or remove comparator categories after observing their results unless the protocol is versioned and the original result remains reproducible.
Do not redefine first from monthly timing to annual rate after observing outcomes.
Do not use release date as event date; score by reference period.
Do not treat energy itself as a downstream comparator because it is part of the initiating shock rather than a downstream consumer category.
Do not convert intermediate mechanism support into terminal ordering support.
